source: MAFF/GIZ, "Guidelines for Banana Export from Cambodia to China" (2022), sections 2.1-2.3
text:
Cambodia's banana exports to China benefit from two layers of trade agreement: the region-wide ASEAN-China Free Trade Agreement, and Cambodia's own bilateral trade arrangements with China, both of which reduce or eliminate tariffs on qualifying agricultural exports. These agreements lower the cost side of exporting, but they do not by themselves grant permission to export a given fresh produce item — that permission is separate and is controlled through China's General Administration of Customs (GACC) phytosanitary approval process.

Fresh banana specifically received this phytosanitary market access approval from China in 2019, under a bilateral protocol between Cambodia's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF) and GACC. Only products that have gone through this product-by-product approval process, and only orchards/packing houses that are individually registered under it, are legally allowed to export to China; a farmer or company cannot simply rely on the general trade agreements to ship banana (or any other fresh fruit) to China without this separate phytosanitary registration. China publishes an official market access list showing which countries and products currently have this approval, which Cambodian exporters can check to confirm current status.
